html:
Ifat was a Muslim sultanate in the eastern Ethiopian highlands and the lowlands toward the Gulf of Aden, ruled by the Walashma dynasty from about 1285 to the early 1400s. The map shows it in its 1200 snapshot, a little before the sultanate itself began, when the older Sultanate of Showa held much of the same ground.

Ifat grew rich on the trade between the highlands and the port of Zeila, and it took over Showa in the 1280s. Its great rival was the Christian Ethiopian Empire of the Solomonic kings, and the two fought over the trade routes. Emperor Amda Seyon defeated Ifat in 1332 and made it pay tribute.

In the early 1400s Sultan Sa'ad ad-Din II was killed near Zeila, and his sons fled to Yemen. They came back to found Adal, which carried on the war and, under Ahmad Gragn, almost conquered Ethiopia in the 1500s.
